entries.name: Apache OpenDAL
entries.use_for: One API to access S3, GCS, Azure, filesystems and 50+ storage services
entries.why: Apache project with bindings for many languages; avoids vendor lock-in in storage code.
entries.summary: Open Data Access Layer giving a unified API over object storage, file storage, SaaS, databases and key-value services. Bindings exist for many languages.
entries.best_for: Storage-agnostic code that must work with S3, GCS, Azure, local filesystems and 50+ services without vendor lock-in.
entries.not_for: Lowest-common-denominator abstraction; provider-specific advanced features may not be exposed. Binding maturity varies by language.

entries.name: Ceph
entries.use_for: Unified distributed object, block and file storage at scale
entries.why: Proven large-scale open storage with an S3-compatible gateway; LGPL licensed.

license_verified.note: COPYING: core under LGPL-2.1 or LGPL-3, some files BSD/MIT

entries.summary: Scalable distributed storage system providing object, block and file storage from one cluster, including an S3-compatible gateway.
entries.best_for: Large self-hosted storage clusters needing unified object, block and file storage.
entries.not_for: Operationally heavy and complex for small setups; consider lighter S3 stores for small clusters. LGPL licensed.

entries.name: Dropzone
entries.use_for: Add drag-and-drop uploads with previews to any web page without a framework.
entries.why: Long-standing, framework-free uploader with progress bars and chunking.
entries.summary: Framework-free library that turns any HTML element into a drag-and-drop zone with file previews, progress bars and XHR uploads. Written in TypeScript with bundled types.
entries.best_for: Adding quick drag-and-drop uploads to plain HTML or any framework.
entries.not_for: Not a headless React hook and no built-in resumable uploads; for those use Uppy or tus. Styling and server handling are your responsibility.

entries.name: FilePond
entries.use_for: Add a polished drag-and-drop file upload field with image previews.
entries.why: Smooth UX, plugin system for image editing/validation and adapters for React, Vue and Svelte.
entries.summary: JavaScript file upload library with drag and drop, image previews and a plugin system for validation and editing, optimizing images before upload. Adapters for React, Vue, Angular, Svelte and jQuery.
entries.best_for: Polished upload fields with image previews and client-side processing.
entries.not_for: Needs a server endpoint to receive uploads; v5 is alpha, and advanced image editing (Pintura) is a separate paid product.

entries.name: Flysystem
entries.use_for: Filesystem abstraction for PHP: local, S3, SFTP and more behind one API
entries.why: Powers the Laravel Storage facade; the standard PHP storage layer.
entries.summary: PHP filesystem abstraction providing one interface over local disks, S3, SFTP and other filesystems via adapters, avoiding vendor lock-in.
entries.best_for: PHP and Laravel apps that need to swap or combine storage backends.
entries.not_for: PHP only; not a file upload or media-processing library. Adapter-specific features may be limited.

entries.name: formidable
entries.use_for: Parse multipart form data and file uploads in any Node.js server.
entries.why: Streaming, framework-agnostic parser with a long track record and wide usage.
entries.summary: Streaming Node.js module for parsing form data, especially multipart file uploads, independent of any web framework.
entries.best_for: Parsing multipart uploads in any Node server, including plain http servers.
entries.not_for: Backend parsing only; no UI or storage handling. Express users often prefer Multer.

entries.name: Garage
entries.use_for: Run lightweight S3-compatible storage across a few self-hosted machines.
entries.why: Designed for small, geo-distributed clusters on modest hardware; simple to operate (AGPL-3.0).
entries.summary: S3-compatible distributed object storage designed for small-to-medium self-hosted, geo-distributed clusters. Replicates data across locations and stays available when nodes fail, with a focus on being lightweight and easy to operate.
entries.best_for: Self-hosting S3 storage across a few modest machines or sites.
entries.not_for: Not aimed at very large data-center scale or the full S3 feature surface; licensed AGPL-3.0.

entries.name: JuiceFS
entries.use_for: POSIX distributed file system on top of object storage and Redis/SQL metadata
entries.why: Mount S3 as a shared, fast filesystem for apps and ML workloads; Apache-2.0.
entries.summary: High-performance POSIX file system for cloud-native environments, storing data in object storage such as S3 and metadata in Redis, MySQL, TiKV or similar databases.
entries.best_for: Mounting object storage as a shared filesystem for ML, big data and applications without code changes.
entries.not_for: Requires running a separate metadata engine and object store; operational complexity versus plain S3 access.

entries.name: Laravel Media Library
entries.use_for: Associate uploaded files with Eloquent models, with conversions and responsive images
entries.why: The go-to Laravel upload and media package.
entries.summary: Laravel package that associates files with Eloquent models. Handles uploads, collections, conversions (thumbnails) and responsive images, with storage on any Laravel filesystem.
entries.best_for: Laravel apps attaching images and documents to models.
entries.not_for: Laravel/PHP only; not a general storage or CDN service.

entries.name: Multer
entries.use_for: Handle multipart/form-data file uploads in Express apps.
entries.why: The standard Express upload middleware, maintained by the Express team.
entries.summary: Express middleware for handling multipart/form-data file uploads, built on busboy.
entries.best_for: Express apps receiving file uploads on the server.
entries.not_for: Only processes multipart forms and is Express/Connect specific; no resumable uploads or client UI.

entries.name: rclone
entries.use_for: Sync, copy and mount files across 70+ cloud storage providers
entries.why: The Swiss-army knife for cloud storage; also usable as a Go library or via its remote-control HTTP API.
entries.summary: Command-line program to sync, copy and mount files across 70+ cloud storage providers. Supports hash checking, bisync, check mode, encryption and a remote-control API.
entries.best_for: Backups and migrations between cloud storages, or mounting cloud storage on a machine.
entries.not_for: CLI tool, not an embedded app storage SDK for typical web requests; not a file-upload component.

entries.name: react-dropzone
entries.use_for: Add a drag-and-drop file zone to a React app with a hook.
entries.why: Tiny, headless hook-based API that is the go-to dropzone for React.
entries.summary: Simple React hook (useDropzone) and component for HTML5-compliant drag-and-drop file zones. Headless and tiny.
entries.best_for: React apps needing a customizable drop zone UI.
entries.not_for: React only and only collects files; no uploading, previews or progress built in.

entries.name: RustFS
entries.use_for: Self-host S3-compatible object storage written in Rust.
entries.why: Apache-2.0 MinIO alternative with a quickly growing community and a web console.
entries.summary: High-performance distributed object storage in Rust with broad S3 API compatibility, a web console and Apache-2.0 license, targeting data lakes and AI workloads.
entries.best_for: Self-hosted S3 storage, particularly as a permissively licensed MinIO alternative.
entries.not_for: Newer project with partial S3 compatibility (supported features only); verify maturity and features before production.

entries.name: SeaweedFS
entries.use_for: Self-host distributed object storage with an S3 API for many small or large files.
entries.why: Mature, fast store for billions of files with S3, FUSE and WebDAV access.
entries.summary: Distributed file system for storing billions of files with O(1) access. One weed binary serves S3 object storage, POSIX/FUSE, WebDAV and more, with cloud tiering.
entries.best_for: Self-hosted storage for many small files or large scale with an S3 API.
entries.not_for: Multi-component setup (master, volume, filer) takes learning; some advanced features are enterprise-only.

entries.name: Shrine
entries.use_for: Handle file attachments and uploads in Ruby and Rails apps.
entries.why: Modular toolkit with direct-to-S3 uploads, background processing and derivatives.
entries.summary: Ruby toolkit for file attachments with a modular plugin system, streaming uploads, cloud storage (S3, GCS, Cloudinary) and integrations with Sequel, ActiveRecord, ROM, Hanami and Mongoid.
entries.best_for: Ruby and Rails apps wanting flexible uploads, direct-to-S3 and background processing.
entries.not_for: Ruby only; requires assembling plugins, which is more setup than Active Storage.

entries.name: Supabase Storage
entries.use_for: Self-host an S3-compatible storage API with Postgres-backed metadata and row-level security.
entries.why: Powers Supabase Storage; brings Postgres policies to file access and supports resumable uploads.
entries.summary: Object storage service using Postgres for metadata and row level security policies for authorization. Supports HTTP, TUS resumable uploads, an S3-compatible API and Iceberg REST catalog.
entries.best_for: Self-hosting storage with Postgres-driven access control, especially alongside Supabase.
entries.not_for: Designed around Postgres and the Supabase stack; not a standalone drop-in without that infrastructure.

entries.name: tus-js-client
entries.use_for: Resumable file uploads from browsers and Node using the tus protocol
entries.why: Official tus client pairing with tusd; reliable large uploads that survive network drops.
entries.summary: Pure JavaScript client for the tus resumable upload protocol, running in browsers, Node.js, React Native and Cordova. Uploads can pause and resume after interruptions.
entries.best_for: Reliable large-file uploads that survive network drops, paired with a tus server such as tusd.
entries.not_for: Needs a tus-compatible server; no UI included, so use Uppy for a dashboard.

entries.name: tusd
entries.use_for: Run a server for resumable uploads using the open tus protocol.
entries.why: Reference tus server with S3, GCS and Azure storage backends; pairs with Uppy and tus-js-client.
entries.summary: Official reference server for the tus resumable upload protocol, with storage backends including local disk, S3, GCS and Azure.
entries.best_for: Hosting a resumable upload endpoint for large files, used with tus-js-client or Uppy.
entries.not_for: Only does uploading, not file processing or serving; written in Go and needs a client that speaks tus.

entries.name: UploadThing
entries.use_for: Type-safe file uploads for full-stack TypeScript apps (Next.js, Remix, etc.)
entries.why: Popular DX-first upload SDK with React components and server routes.
entries.summary: SDK for type-safe file uploads in full-stack TypeScript apps (Next.js, Remix and others), with server route definitions and React components. Uploads run through the UploadThing hosted service.
entries.best_for: TypeScript apps wanting uploads with minimal setup and good developer experience.
entries.not_for: Primarily tied to the UploadThing service for storage; README is minimal, so check pricing and self-hosting before committing.

entries.name: Uppy
entries.use_for: Add a modular file uploader with drag and drop, remote sources and resumable uploads.
entries.why: Most complete JS uploader: tus, S3 multipart, Dashboard UI and Companion for Google Drive/Dropbox imports.
entries.summary: Modular JavaScript file uploader with a Dashboard UI. Fetches files from disk, URLs, Google Drive, Dropbox, Box or camera, previews them and uploads with tus, S3 multipart or XHR.
entries.best_for: Full-featured uploads with remote sources and resumable large files.
entries.not_for: Larger than simple dropzones; remote providers need the Companion server. Overkill for a basic file input.
